cards.explanation: The answer is his enemy. Jesus says, “…his enemy came and sowed weeds among the wheat, and slipped away.” (Matthew 13:25) Everybody's asleep, and somebody's out there doing the most unneighborly thing in history. No name tag, no note, just weeds.

The answer is weeds. The enemy sowed weeds among the wheat. The seed was the wheat's whole future, and he went and stuck weeds right in the middle of it. When the weeds appear, the servants ask, “Where then did the weeds come from?” (Matthew 13:27)

The answer is False, friends. Jesus says, “When the wheat sprouted and bore grain, then the weeds also appeared.” The wheat was already up and growing, and then the weeds showed up. It's the kind of surprise where everything looks fine, right up until it doesn't.

The answer is True, friends. The servants ask if they should pull the weeds, and the owner says, “No.” His instruction is, “Let both grow together until the harvest.” That's not what you'd expect a farmer to say, and it makes you want to hear why.

The answer is that they might uproot the wheat too, friends. The owner says, “if you pull the weeds now, you might uproot the wheat with them.” He's thinking about the good crop. Pull the wrong thing, and you lose what you were trying to protect.

The answer is False, friends. The owner says, “First collect the weeds and tie them in bundles to be burned; then gather the wheat into my barn.” Weeds first, wheat second. The wheat ends up in the barn at the end.

The answer is that they will be burned. The owner says the weeds are collected and tied in bundles “…to be burned…” They're not wheat, and they don't go where the wheat goes. The wheat goes into his barn.

The answer is a tree, friends. Jesus says, “…it grows into the largest of garden plants and becomes a tree…” The smallest seed ends up as the largest garden plant. Not bad for something you could lose on your fingertip.

The answer is True, friends. Jesus says the mustard plant grows big enough that “…the birds of the air come and nest in its branches.” Think about that. The seed started so small, and now it's big enough to be a home for birds.

The answer is leaven, friends, and now we're in my kitchen. A woman takes it and mixes it into three measures of flour, “…until all of it was leavened.” (Matthew 13:33) In the dough business, you know leaven in the right place changes the whole batch.
The answer is all of it. Jesus says the leaven is mixed in “…until all of it was leavened.” It doesn't skip a corner of the bowl. The whole batch is changed.

The answer is False. Matthew says, “Jesus spoke all these things to the crowds in parables. He did not tell them anything without using a parable.” Every bit of it was a parable. Nothing was left out.

The answer is the weeds in the field, friends. The disciples come to Jesus and say, “Explain to us the parable of the weeds in the field.” They don't ask about the other two. This is the one they want explained.

The answer is the sons of the evil one, friends. Jesus says, “The weeds are the sons of the evil one…” The good seed represents the sons of the kingdom, and the weeds are not the same crop. Jesus is spelling out what each piece of the parable stands for.
The answer is True, friends. Jesus says, “…the enemy who sows them is the devil.” So the sneaky one who slipped away from the field gets a name. Jesus doesn't leave you guessing.
The answer is angels. Jesus says, “…the harvesters are angels.” So when the owner in the parable tells the harvesters what to do, Jesus says angels are the ones doing it.

The answer is False. Jesus says, “As the weeds are collected and burned in the fire, so will it be at the end of the age.” It's a heavy line, and I think it's fine to say so. Jesus said it plainly, so we hear it plainly.

The answer is every cause of sin and all who practice lawlessness, friends. Jesus says the angels will “…weed out of His kingdom every cause of sin and all who practice lawlessness.” It's one big sorting job, and it belongs to His angels. That's what He tells the disciples.

The answer is True, and it's a beautiful line, friends. Jesus says, “Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father.” After all that weeding, this is where He lands. Nothing dim about it.
